restated_for_a_rectangle.D1: 'obverse silhouette' -> the obverse's principal device, which on this note is the PORTRAIT VIGNETTE; registered by homography, not by a disc
restated_for_a_rectangle.D2: SPLIT in two per §18.4 (D2a pyramid, D2b eagle) and restated: the device is embedded in ornament with no bare field, so no contour is traceable; the available silhouette is the seal's RIM, found by a curve-following score, and IoU is computed between our drawn roundel and that ellipse. Two further rows fall out that a disc never needs: D2c separation and D2d shape (a circle on the note is an ellipse in our anisotropic box)
restated_for_a_rectangle.D5: there is no band RADIUS. A legend on a rectangle is frozen as PY2's two extremes in Cartesian form — cap-top Y and baseline Y in viewBox units, plus the X extent
restated_for_a_rectangle.D8: there is no field circle. The analogous constraint is the PRINTED BORDER RECTANGLE, the note's own outermost engraved element and the thing §18.1 registers on. A second, tighter locus is added because `struck()` documents rField as omitted for the note: each device against ITS OWN ROUNDEL
restated_for_a_rectangle.D13: 'field' is not bare metal — a note is engraved edge to edge and has no bare region at all, which is why every density instrument tried on this subject returned its own search bound. Field is frozen as a STATISTIC: the 90th-percentile grey inside a frozen window

genuinely_N_A.D1.reverse: D1's metric names the obverse; the reverse's principal devices are scored by D2a/D2b
genuinely_N_A.D7.reverse: D7 applies to paths PRODUCED BY FITTING A CONTOUR (§3's D7 row). Every path on the note's reverse is authored — triangles, arcs and chevrons written by hand in absolute viewBox coordinates. The metric has no subject on this side. Scored whole anyway as evidence: 42 of 48 knots over 75 deg, worst 145.1 (176.9 at icon), and every one of them is a corner the design declares by construction — P1/P2's degenerate-metric case exactly

what_a_rectangle_ADDS_that_the_rubric_ha: ANISOTROPY. A disc has one scale; a rectangle has two, and ours deliberately do not match the note's (31 CFR 411 non-copy). Every position taken from the note must go through a homography, and every CIRCLE on the note must be drawn as an ELLIPSE 1.3145x taller than wide. No rubric row asks whether a shape's aspect matches — D2d had to be invented.
TWO DEVICES ON ONE SIDE. §18.4 already says score them separately; the rubric's one-row-per-side shape fights it, and D2/D13 each needed splitting.

NO FIELD. Every dimension that assumes a bare region against which a device stands (D2's segmentation, D5's band detection, D13's field level) degrades on this subject, and this round watched 60 detector settings return their own bounds because of it.

dimensions.why_escalate_not_pass: ONE artefact can carry this measurement. It needs a sound border fit AND a paper box that is a measurement rather than a crop, and only `bill-rev-2.jpg` has both — `bill-obv.jpg` has a degenerate border fit, `bill-obv-2.jpg` has no real border fit either (R0b_obverse), and `bill-rev.jpg`'s paper runs off the frame (ratio 2.4239 against a true 2.3525). PY1's rule applies: a constant may not be scored until it is measured on every subject that carries it.
dimensions.the_answer_to_the_question_asked: yes, the note has an analogue of EDGE.field, and unlike EDGE.field it turns out to be approximately RIGHT — within half a viewBox unit on every side. The interesting finding is the negative one: this is the first shared-constant audit in the series that did not turn up a 3-unit error.

failing_repairable_in_priority_order.note: the eagle's containment cannot be repaired independently of D2 — the roundel it breaches is 1.80x too wide and in the wrong place, so fixing the roundel changes the breach. They are one job.

failing_repairable_in_priority_order.why: structure before tone (§5). Both roundels are 1.80x too wide, 26% too close together, and circles where the registration requires ellipses at ry/rx 1.314. This is the same 'fill the container rather than fit the design' error §22.5 has now found FIVE times, and it is the top of the note's list in bill.md §7 from the previous pass. Fixing it re-places every path inside both devices, which is why it is one brief and not four.
